why: One place for the caps on every value send out of our Arc/Base wallets (lib/arc-send-gate.js). Root-owned: no bot can raise its own cap. Destinations are copied from data/protected/account/wallet-registry.json, data/arc-apex.json and the senders' own code, each checked on chain (code present for contracts) on 2026-10-06. A sender starts in shadow and moves to enforce only after one full cycle of it ran clean.

destinations.0x53dea4f7783c1de84cecc5c989bc37a5571548: Arc launchpad router (dip-trader.js ROUTER; code 752 bytes)
destinations.0x87b4a0ded942055641d7b7f5812d698e2124d8: our Arc swap router (registry; code 2,517 bytes)

arc-dip-trader.note: 6 Oct: shadow first. Buys go to the launchpad router (0.80 USDC floor size); the faucet share goes to the pot (whatever is owed). Move to enforce after one clean day; then consider separate caps for buys and the share. | 7 Oct: ENFORCE. Evidence: two planted checks with the trader's exact arguments (buy to the launchpad router 0.80, faucet share to the pot) were allowed; the trader is idle (breaker on, 0.23 USDC under its 1 USDC reserve), so no real day of decisions exists. Its gate call now fails closed.

arc-buy-and-rate.note: 6 Oct: pays other Arc agents per call; the payee comes from each agent's own 402, so no fixed list; the caps match the script's own MAX_PER_CALL (0.01) and per-run budget (0.20). | 7 Oct: ENFORCE after a real shadow allow (#232, 0.002 USDC, 04:13 UTC); its gate call now fails closed.
